subject.title: fix(update): dev channel update builds from an unverified checkout at the git install path

question: Should package-to-dev conversion permanently refuse every pre-existing `OPENCLAW_GIT_DIR` destination—including empty directories and canonical OpenClaw checkouts—and require users to move it or select an unused path?
rationale: This is a deliberate tradeoff between preventing execution from an untrusted checkout and changing an existing update/setup path for users with a populated destination; code review cannot choose that compatibility policy safely.

options.title: Approve fail-closed conversion
options.body: Keep refusal of all non-updater-owned destinations, document the one-time operator action, and require final-head proof before merge.

options.title: Preserve a supported reuse path
options.body: Define a narrower trusted migration or explicit user-confirmed path for existing destinations, then revise the security model and tests accordingly.

options.title: Pause the change
options.body: Do not merge until an updater/security owner chooses the permanent conversion contract.

recommendation.title: Approve fail-closed conversion
recommendation.body: Keep refusal of all non-updater-owned destinations, document the one-time operator action, and require final-head proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The PR discussion explicitly routes the updater compatibility decision to this person.
